cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: So, I understand you’re interested in restaurant work?

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yes. I’ve got a bit of experience and I can provide references.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: That’s good. I can check all that later. Now, Milo’s Restaurants have some vacancies at the moment. They’re a really good company to work for. Lots of benefits.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Oh right.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Yes. They’ve got a very good reputation for looking after staff. For example, all employees get training – even temporary staff. Q1

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Oh really? That’s quite unusual, isn’t it?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Certainly is.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: And do staff get free uniforms too?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Um … you just need to wear a white T-shirt and black trousers, it says here. So I guess not … But another benefit of working for a big company like this is that you can get a discount at any of their restaurants. Q2

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Even at weekends?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: No, but you’ll be working then anyway.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Oh yes. I suppose so. Most of their restaurants are in the city centre, aren’t they? So, easy to get to by bus?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Yes. That’s right. But if you have to do a late shift and finish work after midnight, the company will pay for you to get a taxi home. Q3

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: I probably won’t need one. I think I’d use my bike.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: OK. Now, they do have some quite specific requirements for the kind of person they’re looking for. Milo’s is a young, dynamic company and they’re really keen on creating a strong team. It’s really important that you can fit in and get on well with everyone.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yeah. I’ve got no problem with that. It sounds good, actually. The last place I worked for was quite demanding too. We had to make sure we gave a really high level of service. Q4

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: That’s good to hear because that will be equally important at Milo’s. I know they want people who have an eye for detail.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: That’s fine. I’m very used to working in that kind of environment.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Perfect. So the only other thing that’s required is good communication skills, so you’ll need to have a certificate in English. Q5

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Sure.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: OK. Let’s have a look at the current job vacancies at Milo’s. The first one is in Wivenhoe Street. Q6

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Sorry, where?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Wivenhoe. W-l-V-E-N-H-O-E. It’s quite central, just off Cork Street.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Oh right.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: They’re looking for a breakfast supervisor.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: That would be OK.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: So you’re probably familiar with the kind of responsibilities involved. Obviously checking that all the portions are correct, etc., and then things like checking all the procedures for cleaning the equipment are being followed. Q7

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: OK. And what about the salary? In my last job I was getting £9.50 per hour. I was hoping to get a bit more than that.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Well, to begin with, you’d be getting £9.75 but that goes up to £11.25 after three months. Q8

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: That’s not too bad. And I suppose it’s a very early start?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Mmm. That’s the only unattractive thing about this job. But then you have the afternoons and evenings free. So the restaurant starts serving breakfast from 7 a.m. And you’d have to be there at 5.30 to set everything up. But you’d be finished at 12.30.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Mmm. Well, as you say, there are advantages to that.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Now, you might also be interested in the job at the City Road branch. That’s for a junior chef, so again a position of responsibility.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: I might prefer that, actually.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Right, well obviously this role would involve supporting the sous chef and other senior staff. And you’d be responsible for making sure there’s enough stock each week – and sorting out all the deliveries. Q9

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: I’ve never done that before, but I imagine it’s fairly straightforward, once you get the hang of it.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: Yes, and you’d be working alongside more experienced staff to begin with, so I’m sure it wouldn’t be a problem. The salary’s slightly higher here. It’s an annual salary of £23,000.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Right.

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: I know that if they like you, it’s likely you’ll be promoted quite quickly. So that’s worth thinking about.

cues.speaker: MAN
cues.text: Yes. It does sound interesting. What are the hours like?

cues.speaker: WOMAN
cues.text: The usual, I think. There’s a lot of evening and weekend work, but they’re closed on Mondays. But you do get one Sunday off every four weeks. So would you like me to send off your … Q10
